\chapter{Chapter07 — Dictator Testing}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter07.DictatorTesting
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.DictatorTesting}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Nonadaptive Function Tester]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b001}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester}
\leanok
Let the domain and codomain be types and let $r$ be a nonnegative integer. A nonadaptive
function tester consists of a finite seed space with a probability distribution, a rule
that assigns to each seed and each of the $r$ transcript positions either a domain
element to query or no query, and a deterministic rule that decides acceptance from the
seed and the resulting partial transcript of codomain values.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Tester transcript]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester}
For a nonadaptive tester with $r$ query positions, let $f$ map domain elements to
codomain elements and fix a random seed. At each position, its transcript records the
value of $f$ at the queried address if an address is specified, and records no value if
that position has no query.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Transcript at a query position]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript}
\difficulty{1}
Let $T$ be a nonadaptive function tester, let $f$ map its domain to its codomain, let
$s$ be a seed, and let $j$ be a transcript position. The transcript’s entry at $j$ is
the value of $f$ at the query address chosen at position $j$, if that address exists;
otherwise the entry is absent.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tester acceptance]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript}
A nonadaptive tester accepts a function at a given seed if its deterministic acceptance
predicate, applied to that seed and the transcript of the function's answers, returns
true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance probability of a nonadaptive tester]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.pmfExpectation}
Let $T$ be a randomized nonadaptive tester with a finite seed space, a probability law
on its seeds, and a deterministic acceptance rule. For a function $f$ from its domain to
its codomain, its acceptance probability is the probability that the tester accepts the
transcript obtained by answering each queried address using $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rejection probability of a nonadaptive tester]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.rejectionProbability}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.rejectionProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability}
Let $T$ be a randomized nonadaptive tester with a finite seed space, a probability law
on its seeds, and a deterministic acceptance rule. For a function $f$ from its domain to
its codomain, its rejection probability is one minus its acceptance probability.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability upper bound]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability_le_one}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one, FABL.pmfExpectation_mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a nonadaptive function tester with a finite seed space and a probability
distribution on its seeds, and let $f$ be a function from its domain to its codomain.
The probability that $T$ accepts the transcript obtained by querying $f$ is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability_nonneg}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a nonadaptive function tester with a finite seed space and a probability
distribution on its seeds, and let $f$ be a function from its domain to its codomain.
The probability that $T$ accepts the transcript obtained by querying $f$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform sign probabilities]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_sign_eq_one_add_neg_one_eq_one}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_sign_eq_one_add_neg_one_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set and let $f\colon\Omega\to\{−1,1\}$. Under the
uniform distribution on $\Omega$, the probabilities that $f$ equals $1$ and $−1$ sum to
$1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Local Function Tester]
\lean{FABL.IsLocalTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b002}
\label{FABL.IsLocalTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsFar, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.rejectionProbability}
Let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester on a finite nonempty domain with codomain $\eta$, where
equality in the codomain is decidable, and let $P$ be a property of functions from the
domain to the codomain. A real number $\rho$ is a local testing rate if $\rho>0$, every
function satisfying $P$ is accepted with probability $1$, and for every real
$\varepsilon$ with $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$, any function that is $\varepsilon$-far from
every function satisfying $P$ is rejected with probability strictly greater than
$\rho\varepsilon$.
\end{definition}

\proofstep
  {FABL.IsLocalTester}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty domain, let $\beta$ be a finite alphabet, and let $T$
be a nonadaptive tester with a finite seed space and acceptance probability $\Pr[T\text{
accepts }f]$ on each function $f:\Omega\to\beta$. Let $P$ be a property of such
functions and let $\mathrm{rate}\in\mathbb R$. Assume $\mathrm{rate}>0$, every function
in $P$ is accepted with probability $1$, and for each $\delta\in[0,1]$ every function
whose relative Hamming distance from every function in $P$ exceeds $\delta$ has
rejection probability greater than $\mathrm{rate}\,\delta$. If $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ and
$f:\Omega\to\beta$ is accepted with probability at least $1-\mathrm{rate}\,\varepsilon$,
then there exists a function $g\in P$ whose relative Hamming distance from $f$ is at
most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.IsLocalTester}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\beta$ be a codomain, let $T$ be a
randomized nonadaptive tester on functions $\Omega\to\beta$, and let $P$ be a property
of such functions. Suppose its rate $\rho$ is positive, every function satisfying $P$ is
accepted with probability one, and for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ and every function
$f$, acceptance probability at least $1-\rho\varepsilon$ implies that $f$ is within
relative Hamming distance $\varepsilon$ of some function satisfying $P$. Then $T$ is a
local tester for $P$ with rate $\rho$: every function satisfying $P$ is accepted with
probability one, and every function more than $\varepsilon$ away from all functions
satisfying $P$ is rejected with probability greater than $\rho\varepsilon$ for each
$\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Binary Linearity Transcript Acceptance]
\lean{FABL.blrTranscriptAccept}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b003
}
\label{FABL.blrTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
Given three possibly absent answers from $\mathbb{F}_2$, accept if all three are present
and the first two sum to the third; reject if any answer is absent.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Binary Linearity Function Tester]
\lean{FABL.blrFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b003
}
\label{FABL.blrFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.blrTranscriptAccept, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a nonnegative integer $n$, choose a pair $(x,y)$ uniformly from
$(\mathbb{F}_2^n)^2$. Query a function $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ at $x$, $y$,
and $x+y$, and accept exactly when all three answers are present and the first two sum
to the third.
\end{definition}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b004}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:(\mathbb F_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be linear, so
that $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y\in(\mathbb F_2)^n$. The BLR tester that samples a
uniform pair $x,y$ and checks whether $f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)$ accepts with probability $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate Dictator Function]
\lean{FABL.IsDictator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p044-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p175-b003
}
\label{FABL.IsDictator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.dictator}
Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{\pm1\}$. It is a
dictator if there is a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $f$ is the $i$th
coordinate projection.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Dictator on a Specified Coordinate Set]
\lean{FABL.IsDictatorIn}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b006}
\label{FABL.IsDictatorIn}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.dictator}
Let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinate indices, and let $f$ be a function from the
$n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{\pm1\}$. The function $f$ is a dictator on $S$ if it
is the coordinate projection for some index in $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign Linearity Transcript Acceptance]
\lean{FABL.signBlrTranscriptAccept}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b003
}
\label{FABL.signBlrTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
Given three possibly absent answers from $\{\pm1\}$, accept if all three are present
and the product of the first two equals the third; reject if any answer is absent.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign-valued BLR tester]
\lean{FABL.signBlrFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p159-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b003
}
\label{FABL.signBlrFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.signBlrTranscriptAccept, FABL.uniformPMF}
For each $n\ge 0$, define a three-query tester on sign-valued functions on the Boolean
cube. It samples $x,y\in\mathbb F_2^n$ independently and uniformly, queries the function
at the sign-embedded points corresponding to $x$, $y$, and $x+y$, and applies the sign
BLR transcript acceptance rule to the three answers.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sign BLR acceptance characterization]
\lean{FABL.signBlr_accepts_iff_blrAccepts}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p032-b004}
\label{FABL.signBlr_accepts_iff_blrAccepts}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.blrAccepts, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.signBlrFunctionTester, FABL.signBlrTranscriptAccept, FABL.signEncode_add, FABL.signEncode_booleanFunctionF₂Encoding}
\difficulty{3}
For any $n\ge 0$, function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and $x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the
sign BLR tester accepts $f$ on seed $(x,y)$ if and only if its binary encoding
$g:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ satisfies $g(x)+g(y)=g(x+y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability of the sign BLR tester]
\lean{FABL.signBlrFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.signBlrFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.blrAcceptanceProbability, FABL.blrAccepts, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.signBlrFunctionTester, FABL.signBlrTranscriptAccept, FABL.signBlr_accepts_iff_blrAccepts, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{5}
For any $n\ge 0$ and any function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, the acceptance probability
of the tester that samples independent uniform $x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, queries $f$ at
the sign encodings of $x$, $y$, and $x+y$, and accepts when the first two answers
multiply to the third, equals the BLR acceptance probability of the function
$g:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ obtained by transporting $f$ through the
coordinatewise sign encoding.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign of a Coordinate Sum]
\lean{FABL.signEncode_coordinateSum_local}
\label{FABL.signEncode_coordinateSum_local}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.coordinateSum, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signEncode_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of the coordinates
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $x$ assign an element of $\mathbb{F}_2$ to each
coordinate. The sign encoding of the sum in $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the coordinates of $x$ in
$S$ equals the product of their sign encodings.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.signEncode_coordinateSum_local}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p031-b002}
For every $n$ and every set $S$ of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the parity sign on
binary inputs, transported to the sign cube by the coordinatewise binary-to-sign
correspondence, equals the product of the input signs over $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distance under binary encoding]
\lean{FABL.relativeHammingDist_booleanFunctionF₂Encoding_coordinateSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryParitySign, FABL.binaryParitySign_transport_eq_parityFunction, FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.coordinateSum, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signEncode_booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_ne_eq_relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$, and let $S$ be a set of
its coordinates. The relative Hamming distance between the binary encoding of $f$ and
the sum modulo $2$ of the coordinates in $S$ equals the relative Hamming distance
between $f$ and the product of the sign coordinates in $S$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.relativeHammingDist_booleanFunctionF₂Encoding_coordinateSum}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p031-b002}
Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ and $\eta\in\mathbb R$. If the sign-valued BLR
tester accepts $f$ with probability at least $1-\eta$, then some parity function on the
cube differs from $f$ on at most an $\eta$ fraction of inputs.
\end{theorem}

dictator function $f(x)=x_i$ with probability $1$.

\begin{definition}[Not-all-equal transcript acceptance]
\lean{FABL.naeTranscriptAccept}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p175-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p176-b001
}
\label{FABL.naeTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsNAE3, FABL.Sign}
Given three optional signs, accept exactly when all three are present and their values
are not all equal; reject if any value is absent.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Not-all-equal voting tester]
\lean{FABL.naeFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p175-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p176-b001
}
\label{FABL.naeFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.RankingProfile, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.naeTranscriptAccept, FABL.pairwiseVotes, FABL.uniformPMF}
For each $n\ge 0$, define a three-query tester on sign-valued functions on the Boolean
cube. It samples a ranking profile uniformly, queries the function at the three
pairwise-vote sign vectors specified by that profile, and accepts exactly when all three
answers are present and are not all equal.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance and Condorcet probability]
\lean{FABL.naeFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.naeFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsNAE3, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.condorcetWinnerIndicator_eq_nae3, FABL.condorcetWinnerProbability, FABL.nae3Indicator, FABL.naeFunctionTester, FABL.naeTranscriptAccept, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.societalOutcome, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean social choice
function. Choose each of $n$ voters' rankings of three candidates uniformly from the six
possible strict rankings, form the three pairwise vote vectors, and apply $f$ to each;
the three resulting pairwise outcomes are accepted when they are not all equal. The
tester's acceptance probability equals the probability that the resulting societal
outcome has a Condorcet winner.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Signed dictators are always accepted]
\lean{FABL.naeFunctionTester_complete_signedDictator}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p176-b001}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p176-b001}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a coordinate, and choose
whether to negate its sign. The three-way ranking test accepts the signed dictator that
outputs this coordinate, with the chosen negation, with probability $1$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.naeFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p175-b006,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p176-b001}
Let $n>0$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. If $\varepsilon\ge 0$ and the three-way
ranking test accepts $f$ with probability $1-\varepsilon$, then there are a coordinate
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and a choice of whether to negate it such that the relative Hamming
distance from $f$ to that signed dictator is at most $7205\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier weight bound away from level one]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_add_coeff_sq_le_one_of_card_ne_one}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_one_add_coeff_sq_le_one_of_card_ne_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_eq_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ and let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ have cardinality
different from $1$. For $T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, write $\widehat f(T)=\mathbb
E_x[f(x)\prod_{i\in T}x_i]$, where $x$ is uniform on the sign cube, and let
$W_1(f)=\sum_{|T|=1}\widehat f(T)^2$. Then $W_1(f)+\widehat f(S)^2\le 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exists dictator close of sign blr and nae acceptance ge]
\lean{FABL.exists_dictator_close_of_signBlr_and_nae_acceptance_ge}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p176-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p176-b005
}

\begin{definition}[Conjunction of function testers]
\lean{FABL.andFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p175-b004}
\label{FABL.andFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester}
Given two nonadaptive testers with the same domain and codomain, making $r$ and $s$
queries respectively, define a tester making $r+s$ queries. It samples a seed from each
tester according to their respective laws, independently, concatenates their query
lists, and accepts exactly when both testers accept the corresponding blocks of answers.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability of a conjunction tester]
\lean{FABL.andFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.andFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.andFunctionTester, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_bind, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_map, FABL.pmfExpectation_mul_const}
\difficulty{6}
Let $T$ and $U$ be nonadaptive testers for functions from a domain to a codomain, using
respectively $r$ and $s$ queries, and let $f$ be such a function. The tester that runs
both testers with independent seeds and accepts exactly when both accept has acceptance
probability on $f$ equal to the product of their individual acceptance probabilities.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Uniform mixture of function testers]
\lean{FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b004
}
\label{FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.uniformPMF}
Let $t>0$, and let $T_i$ for $i\in\{0,\ldots,t-1\}$ be nonadaptive testers with the same
domain, codomain, and number of queries. Define a tester by choosing $i$ uniformly,
sampling a seed according to $T_i$'s seed law, and then using $T_i$'s queries and
acceptance rule.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability of a uniform tester mixture]
\lean{FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.pmfExpectation_bind, FABL.pmfExpectation_map, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester}
\difficulty{3}
Let $t>0$, and let $T_1,\ldots,T_t$ be nonadaptive function testers with the same
domain, codomain, and number of query positions. For any function $f$ from that domain
to that codomain, the acceptance probability of the tester obtained by choosing one of
these testers uniformly and then using its seed distribution equals the uniform average
of their individual acceptance probabilities on $f$.
\end{theorem}

  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b004}
Let $t>0$, and let $T_0,\ldots,T_{t-1}$ be nonadaptive testers with the same domain,
codomain, and number of queries. For a function $f$ and real numbers $\mathrm{rate}$ and
$\varepsilon$, if the uniform mixture of these testers accepts $f$ with probability at
least $1-(\mathrm{rate}/t)\varepsilon$, then every component $T_i$ accepts $f$ with
probability at least $1-\mathrm{rate}\,\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Uniform BLR and voting tester mixture]
\lean{FABL.blrNaeFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b001}
\label{FABL.blrNaeFunctionTester}

For each $n\ge 0$, define a three-query tester by choosing with equal probability
between the sign-valued BLR tester and the not-all-equal voting tester on the Boolean
cube.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Subset indicator sign vector]
\lean{FABL.subsetIndicatorSign}
\label{FABL.subsetIndicatorSign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube}
For a subset $S$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, define a sign vector on $n$ coordinates by
assigning $-1$ to coordinates in $S$ and $1$ to coordinates outside $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local correction transcript acceptance]
\lean{FABL.localCorrectionTranscriptAccept}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b007}
\label{FABL.localCorrectionTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
Given three optional signs, accept exactly when the first two are present and their
product is $-1$; reject otherwise. The third value does not affect acceptance.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Subset local correction tester]
\lean{FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b007}
\label{FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.localCorrectionTranscriptAccept, FABL.subsetIndicatorSign, FABL.uniformPMF}
For each $n\ge 0$ and each subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define a three-query
tester on sign-valued functions on the Boolean cube. It samples a Boolean-cube point $y$
uniformly, queries at the sign-embedded points corresponding to $y$ and $x+y$, where $x$
is the sign embedding of the indicator vector of $S$, and leaves the third query unused.
It accepts exactly when the first two answers are present and have product $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Correctness probability under Hamming closeness]
\lean{FABL.subsetLocalCorrection_correctProbability_ge}
\label{FABL.subsetLocalCorrection_correctProbability_ge}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsClose, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryParitySign, FABL.binaryParitySign_transport_eq_parityFunction, FABL.localCorrection, FABL.localCorrection_successProbability, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.subsetIndicatorSign, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_ne_eq_relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S,A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let
$f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and let $\delta\in\mathbb{R}$. If the relative Hamming
distance from $f$ to the parity function indexed by $A$ is at most $\delta$, then the
uniform probability over $y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that the local correction of $z\mapsto
f(\phi(z))$, at $x=\phi^{-1}(s_S)$ and $y$, equals the parity function indexed by $A$
evaluated at $s_S$ is at least $1-2\delta$. Here $\phi$ is the coordinatewise
binary-to-sign bijection and $s_S$ is $-1$ on $S$ and $1$ off $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability of the local correction tester]
\lean{FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.localCorrection, FABL.localCorrectionTranscriptAccept, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.subsetIndicatorSign, FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
For every dimension $n$, subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and Boolean function
$f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, the tester's acceptance probability equals the uniform
probability over $y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that the local correction of the function
$z\mapsto f(\phi(z))$ at $x=\phi^{-1}(s_S)$ and $y$ is $-1$, where $\phi$ is the
coordinatewise binary-to-sign bijection and $s_S$ is $-1$ on $S$ and $1$ off $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Dictator subclass tester]
\lean{FABL.dictatorSubclassFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b007
}
\label{FABL.dictatorSubclassFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.blrNaeFunctionTester, FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester, FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester}
For a finite set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the dictator subclass function tester is
the uniform mixture of the three-query BLR linearity tester and the
subset-local-correction tester associated with $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Local testing of a dictator subclass]
\lean{FABL.dictatorSubclass_isLocalTester}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b007
}
\label{FABL.dictatorSubclass_isLocalTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsDictatorIn, FABL.IsLocalTester, FABL.IsLocalTester.close_of_acceptanceProbability_ge, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.Sign, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.blrNaeFunctionTester, FABL.blrNae_isLocalTester, FABL.component_acceptanceProbability_ge_of_uniformMixture_ge, FABL.dictator, FABL.dictatorSubclassFunctionTester, FABL.isLocalTester_of_close_of_acceptanceProbability_ge, FABL.localCorrection, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.subsetIndicatorSign, FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester, FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability, FABL.subsetLocalCorrectionFunctionTester_dictator, FABL.subsetLocalCorrection_correctProbability_ge, FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_sign_eq_one_add_neg_one_eq_one}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates. The tester
formed by choosing uniformly between the BLR–NAE tester and the local correction tester
for $S$ has positive rate $1/100$: it accepts every function equal to a coordinate
projection on some coordinate in $S$ with probability $1$, and, for every
$0\leq\varepsilon\leq1$, it rejects with probability greater than $\varepsilon/100$
every function whose relative Hamming distance from each such coordinate projection is
greater than $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}
